structure.heading: Market Benchmarking Methodology and Pay Band Positioning (2025 Survey Cut)
text_content: **Market Benchmarking Methodology and Pay Band Positioning (2025 Survey Cut)**

The market benchmark for this analysis is the Radford Global Technology Survey 2025 H1 cut, applied with an effective date of 2025-03-01. Job-to-benchmark mapping used Radford job families and skill clusters; incumbents were aligned to the closest Radford benchmark using title, responsibilities, and location adjustments. Base salary market percentiles (P50, P25, P75) were retrieved from the cut and utilized without inflation adjustments. All comparisons reference midpoint-to-market calculations so that band midpoints are directly compared to Radford P50 values for consistent positioning. This approach preserves market consistency.

Across the 112 benchmarked roles included in the study, 38 roles (33.9%) have current midpoint-to-market P50 ratios below 0.95, indicating material underpositioning against market median. The shortfall is concentrated in technical individual contributor and mid-career engineering tracks, while senior leadership and specialized research grades show closer alignment. Role-level variances were quantified so compensation owners can prioritize where to investigate retention impact. The data snapshot date for these role-level findings aligns with the overall analysis timeline and supports targeted corrections referenced elsewhere. Findings are dated 2025-04-15 inclusive.

The aggregated measurement uses a weighted midpoint-to-market P50 metric, calculated by applying incumbent counts and band midpoints to Radford P50 benchmarks, yielding an overall weighted ratio of 0.97 as of 2025-04-15. Weighting privileges headcount exposure so large-population bands drive the consolidated view, which therefore reflects enterprise-level positioning rather than isolated role anomalies. A 0.97 overall ratio signals a modest market lag relative to the median; it informs budget prioritization and indicates that while systemic underpositioning exists, concentrated interventions can align at-risk cohorts more efficiently at scale.

Limitations and governance considerations are important when interpreting the 2025 H1 cut results and the 2025-03-01 effective date. The Radford dataset reflects base salary market positioning; total cash, equity, and benefits require supplemental market inputs and localized cost-of-living adjustments. Currency exchange conventions and geography-specific pay differentials were normalized but remain sensitivity points. Recommended next steps include formalizing a quarterly refresh cadence, documenting job-to-benchmark mapping rules, and establishing an approval workflow for any FY2025 implementation actions to ensure transparent, auditable adjustments aligned with enterprise compensation policy reqs..

structure.heading: Attrition Risk Hotspots and Recommended Salary Band and Equity Corrections (FY2025 Implementation)
text_content: **Attrition Risk Hotspots and Recommended Salary Band and Equity Corrections (FY2025 Implementation)**

Analysis identified concentrated attrition-risk hotspots within critical disciplines: engineering, product, sales operations and customer success. The top 10 attrition-risk roles account for 27 regretted exits in the last 12 months ending 2025-04-30, with these departures concentrated in mid- to senior-level individual contributors. Regretted exits are defined as voluntary departures of incumbents with high performance or critical knowledge. These data were triangulated with exit interviews and manager feedback to confirm that loss severity and frequency in these roles materially exceeds organizational averages and strategic continuity.

Market positioning analysis shows that pay band placement and midpoints for several of the hotspot roles lag external benchmarks, correlating with elevated turnover. Internal compa-ratios and external percentile gaps indicate under-market positioning between the 25th and 50th percentiles for affected roles, amplified by competitive demand for specialized skills. Non-compensation factors (career path clarity, manager effectiveness) were considered, but quantitative alignmnet with survey pricing explains the largest share of attrition variance in the impacted cohorts during the assessment period. This insight guided targeted actions immediately.

To address compensation-driven risk, recommended adjustments increase 6 pay band midpoints by +6.0% to +12.0% effective 2025-07-01. The six targeted bands span mid-career technical ICs, senior product specialists, and selected sales and customer success levels. Implementation will proceed via a single-cycle payroll adjustment on the July 2025 compensation run, with calibrations validated by Total Rewards and Finance. Impact modelling projects a reduction in salary-related attrition probability among affected incumbents within six months, and the adjustments are subject to post-implementation review with governance oversight assigned.

Equity correction actions target pay inequities identified in the affected populations and cover 41 employees with an estimated annualiesd cost of $620,000. Corrections are prioritized by severity, performance status, and time-in-role, with highest priority cases processed in the July 2025 adjustment cycle and remaining cases completed by Q3 FY2025. Funding will be coordinated between People & Culture and Finance, with a dedicated ledger to ensure transparency. Success metrics include a measurable decerase in regretted exits among corrected incumbents and quarterly monitoring through 2025-12-31 reporting.
